title: Analysis of the biological characteristics and gene function of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii
content:
by Yi Wu, Chunlei Zhang, Mengjie Luo, Feng Hai, Xianhua Liu, Xian Jin

The biological characteristics, morphology, and genomic information of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii, isolated from the vaginal secretions of pregnant women, have not yet been reported. Elucidating its biological properties and genetic functions may provide a theoretical foundation for developing probiotic preparations to treat bacterial vaginosis. The strain was identified as L. delbrueckii subsp. sunkii using mass spectrometry and 16S ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA) gene sequencing. Colony morphology was observed, Gram staining characteristics were examined, and cellular ultrastructure was visualized via scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Whole-genome sequencing was performed using both second- and third-generation sequencing platforms, followed by comprehensive bioinformatics analysis. Additionally, biochemical experiments, H2O2 production tests, acid production assays, antibacterial activity assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility tests were conducted. The strain is a Gram-positive, rod-shaped, facultative anaerobe that possesses sparse filamentous, white, spine-like pili on its surface. It efficiently ferments sugars to produce acid but does not produce H2O2. While susceptible to 7 common antibiotics, it is resistant to sulfonamides. It inhibits the growth of Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Streptococcus agalactiae, and produces α-hemolytic rings on blood agar. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) and Clusters of Orthologous Groups (COG) annotations indicated that the strain is primarily involved in metabolic pathways. The Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) annotated 10 antibiotic resistance genes, including those for macrolides, tetracyclines, peptides, lincosamides, glycopeptides, penams, fluoroquinolones, streptogramins, nitroimidazoles, and pleuromutilins. L. delbrueckii subsp. sunkii exhibits strain-dependent variations in morphology, biochemical reactions, and nucleotide sequences. H2O2 production is not a universal feature among strains of this subspecies. It exhibits strong acid production from sugars and high susceptibility to most antibiotics, but shows a genotype-phenotype discrepancy in resistance, as sulfonamides do not inhibit its growth. These findings suggest that this subspecies may be associated with human metabolism and vaginal microbiota balance. However, further animal studies are needed to confirm its functional significance in the human vaginal environment.
